protections: Config-write key denylist: every key collected from `git config` positionals, inline `-c`/`--config`/`--config-env` and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT env is matched against preventUnsafeConfig before any child process is spawned (packages/argv-parser/src/vulnerabilities/detect-vulnerable-config-writes.ts:4-15,39-72; packages/argv-parser/src/config/analyse-config.ts:52-85; packages/argv-parser/src/env/parse-env.ts:31-41).

Command-line flag denylist: every parsed global/task flag name is matched against preventUnsafeFlags and reported with the unsafe category the caller must opt into (packages/argv-parser/src/vulnerabilities/detect-vulnerable-flags.ts:4-16,65-79).

Tokeniser option schema: which short clusters expand into individual switches and which long switches consume the next token is declared per command in flag-specs.ts, so a switch the table does not know reaches the flag denylist only as one opaque token or with no value attached (packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/flag-specs.ts:43-102; packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/token-expander.ts:23-65; packages/argv-parser/src/flags/parse-task-flags.ts:48).

Single enforcement point: simple-git's spawn.args plugin throws for every produced vulnerability unless the matching unsafe category is enabled, and every typed task and raw() route funnels through it (simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts:11-21; simple-git/src/git.mjs:189-193).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The docs call the blocks a non-exhaustive safety net that does not protect against every injection or misuse (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:11-12), and trailer.<token>.command is a per-token formatting feature rather than one of the documented command-binary rows, so the key can be argued out of the list.

The rebase -x/--exec half is a separately credited report bundled in the same commit, so it can be dismissed as a different vulnerability than the trailer config key, and the docs only promise known high-risk patterns (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:11-12).

The option table is a lower-level parsing schema rather than a security check, so a single denylist row is argued to be the whole fix; the report does not mention clustered (-qx/-ix) or value-embedded (-xcmd) switch shapes.
A section rename is a structural edit, not a trailer.<token>.cmd write; the report only shows plain key/value writes and the docs cover known patterns only (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:11-12).
A broad /--exec/ or /-x/ matcher appears to cover the push and rebase spellings at once, and a duplicate category or a task-agnostic short-switch rule looks like harmless over-approximation.

`--` is the documented separator for path-like arguments and everything after it is deliberately treated as a path (packages/argv-parser/src/args/parse-argv.types.ts:62-65), which looks outside a config-key denylist; the report is about key classification, not argument separation.

core.alternateRefsCommand is not named by the advisory and only runs when an alternate object store is advertised, so it can be written off as outside the trailer/rebase reports (docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:11-12).

The config-side difftool.<tool>.cmd key is already blocked, so the command-line -x/--extcmd spelling of the same difftool feature looks covered; difftool is also a display command rather than a repository operation.

conflicts.what: A task-agnostic /--exec/ or /^-?x/ row added for rebase also fires for push --exec (already allowUnsafePack), for the --exec-path getter that must stay silent, and for git clean -x / git.clean('dfx'), so the natural broad fix breaks existing behaviour.

To make -x visible inside -qx/-ix clusters the rebase option table must declare the benign sibling switches and keep -s/-X as value-takers; a case-insensitive matcher would turn the legitimate -X <option> into -x.

Both are closed from the same flat array; a coarse row such as preventConfigBuilder('trailer') or a bare 'core' prefix would close them but refuse legitimate trailer.<token>.key/trailer.separators writes and most core.* writes.

fairness_risks: git clean -x and git.clean('dfx') must keep working (simple-git/test/unit/clean.spec.ts:110-112,191-193); a task-agnostic -x rule contradicts it.
git rev-parse --exec-path used as a getter must stay unflagged (packages/argv-parser/test/vulnerability-analysis.spec.ts:218-223; detect-vulnerable-flags.ts:63); a broad /--exec/ rule contradicts it.
git push --exec=<pack> must keep yielding exactly allowUnsafePack (detect-vulnerable-flags.ts:71; vulnerability-analysis.spec.ts:135-144); a second global row produces two vulnerabilities.

git rebase -s <strategy> and -X <option> are legitimate neighbours of -x; the short-option maps are case-sensitive (packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/flag-specs.ts:43-91), so -X must not be treated as -x.

Legitimate trailer.<token>.key/.where/.ifExists/.ifMissing/.layout and trailer.separators writes share the trailer section with the command keys, so the fix must target .cmd/.command only and not the whole trailer namespace.
git config -- <key> <value> is legitimate (it is how names beginning with '-' are written); the separator fix must re-admit positionals after '--' for the config task, not refuse '--' outright.

git clone --config key=value is a legitimate clone option already parsed through the same inline-write path (packages/argv-parser/test/parse-config-inline.spec.ts:45-50; packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/flag-specs.ts:55) and must not be refused wholesale.

design.why: It pairs the one report-described anchor (T1: trailer.<token>.cmd/.command, with the injection-room sibling T7 in the same list) with four hidden judgements in three layers: the separately credited rebase half (T2, carrying T5's coupling and T8's sibling option), the tokeniser schema that only emits -x from clusters (T3), the rename-section operand that records the source section instead of the destination (T4), and the '--' separator that drops config positionals entirely (T6). The reasons to dismiss are all different (non-exhaustive docs, different advisory, lower-level parsing schema, structural edit, path separator), T2/T4/T6 give the deepseek absent-protection-plus-dismissal shape and T3/T5 give the mimo how-type/coupled shape, and T2/T5/T8 force the fix to stay task- and case-specific so git clean -x, push --exec, the --exec-path getter and rebase -X keep working. A design built only from the two published halves is one judgement (append rows to two lists) and is fully derivable from the fix commit; this one also requires reading the parser's separator, operand and tokeniser behaviour.

unverified: The fix commit d762810c13b331ff1e5eb24c0b434646d2a8d1b3 is not present in the pinned worktree; fix_sites and the claim that the fix leaves the rename/separator routes untouched come from the screener lead rather than the patch itself.

Pinned code omits 'config' from the GLOBAL long-option set (packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/flag-specs.ts:31-40) while analyse-config.ts:39 treats '--config' as a write source, so a space-separated global `--config <k=v>` is never collected; whether git accepts that exact global form cannot be checked from the pinned tree, so it is not scored as a trap.
core.alternateRefsCommand's shell-execution semantics are external git behaviour; pinned evidence is only that no row or other guard names it (detect-vulnerable-config-writes.ts:39-72).
git difftool -x/--extcmd and git grep -O/--open-files-in-pager were noticed as further unguarded command-naming options; only difftool -x is recorded as a trap and grep -O was not verified.
No latest release tree was supplied, so present_in_latest/latest_where for T4, T6, T7 and T8 are unknown.
Whether the hidden behavioural tests require a real git binary at runtime; the project's own unit tests drive fixture child-process streams.
